clue.text: Promenade is in a perfect place

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the walk word, so 'in' marks one piece going within another

parts.note: a promenade is a parade, a public walk or procession
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaside walkway is praised as a perfect spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven or an idyllic spot, an ideal location.

clue.text: Fruit father handles roughly

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to paw is to touch or handle clumsily or roughly

explanation.surface: A father is rough with the fruit he picks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaws (pawpaws) are tropical fruits, another name for papayas.

clue.text: Repair broken fencing equipment

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of place, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to mend damaged fencing gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thin-bladed sword used in fencing.

clue.text: Lyric Ted composed in a trice!

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, telling us to rearrange the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A songwriter called Ted dashed off a lyric in no time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, at once, without delay.

clue.text: Ring the girl about something afoot

indicators.note: about means around, so the pronoun for the girl goes around the ring letter

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl
a ring is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl is wearing a ring and there is some intrigue going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something afoot' looks like a plot under way, but literally it is a thing worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is literally worn on a foot; the idiom normally means a scheme is in progress.

clue.text: Novel hat

definitions.meaning: a famous 1894 novel by George du Maurier about the singer Svengali controls
a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and indented crown

explanation.definitionFit: Trilby is a du Maurier novel, and the felt hat took its name from the stage version of that book.

clue.text: Bird entranced by gold?

parts.note: rapt means spellbound or entranced
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A bird seems spellbound by something golden.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a bird of prey such as a hawk or eagle.

clue.text: Gets washing on line — read sun is out!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hangs washing on the line and reads that the sun has come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' rearranges READ SUN into AUNDERS, which follows the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash them, so one who launders is getting the washing done.

clue.text: Producing elastic

definitions.meaning: giving or bringing forth, as a field gives crops

explanation.definitionFit: Yielding means both bearing a crop or return, and being soft and pliant.

clue.text: Probe rigorously into earnings of delivery lad

indicators.note: into means the shuffled letters go inside the word for earnings

parts.note: pay means wages or earnings

indicators.note: rigorously suggests vigorous working over, so the letters of probe are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone investigates what a delivery boy earns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigorously' turns PROBE into PERBO, which 'into' places inside PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperboy is a lad who delivers newspapers.

clue.text: Second petty-officer to employ a mate

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for petty officer, a naval rank
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A second petty officer is hired to be a shipmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' in a naval surface suggests a shipmate, but here it is a partner in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a partner, as a husband or wife is one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Fenced off first early shelter

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters of fenced are rearranged
first picks out the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: An area was fenced off early on to provide shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FENCED into DEFENC, followed by E, the first letter of 'early'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defence is protection, a shield against attack, which is what shelter gives.

clue.text: Emotional pain felt on parting with this appliance

definitions.meaning: a painful separation, the pang of leaving someone
a tool, here a spanner for turning nuts

explanation.surface: Someone is sad to part company with a household gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is both the pang of a painful parting and a gripping tool, an appliance in the old sense of a device.

clue.text: Bound, once again, to be reported?

definitions.meaning: tied up with cord a second time, re- plus corded
set down in writing as an account

explanation.surface: Someone is tied up again and wonders if this will be written up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as RE-CORDED, tied with cord again.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded means put on record, documented, as a report is; read as re-corded it means tied up afresh.

clue.text: Females one can't score off

definitions.meaning: a maiden over in cricket is a set of six balls with no runs scored

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an over is six balls bowled by one player; a maiden is one where no runs come off it. The plural answer suits 'ones', loosely clued as 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens are young women, and in cricket a maiden is an over from which the batsman scores no runs.

clue.text: Put a pound in the hat for food

indicators.note: in places the pound abbreviation within the hat word

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone drops a pound in a hat to pay for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a salted, smoked herring eaten as food, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes flat with a heated appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.definitionFit: To iron is to press clothes, and an iron is a type of golf club.

clue.text: Jacket for a corgi

definitions.meaning: one of the two breeds of Welsh corgi, named after a Welsh county

explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted jacket, and the Cardigan is one breed of Welsh corgi (the other being the Pembroke).

clue.text: Point to a fizzy drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the letters of the words before are stirred up

explanation.surface: A person points someone towards a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' looks like part of the definition but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A potation is a formal or jocular word for a drink, especially alcoholic.

clue.text: Rush Frank's found by murky river

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp it

indicators.note: murky means muddied or unclear, so the letters of the river's name are stirred up

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Frank rushes off and is found beside a muddy river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the verb, to mark post. 'murky' jumbles DEE into EDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden mass rush, as of panicking cattle.

clue.text: Running wild yet claiming to be in order

parts.note: am is a form of the verb to be, as in I am
OK means all right, in good order

explanation.surface: Someone is out of control while insisting all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'I am OK' is claiming to be in order, which gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok means rampaging wildly out of control.

clue.text: Train crash due to beast on top of engine

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of due are rearranged

parts.note: a cat is a beast, an animal

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A train crashed because an animal was sitting on the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway vehicle, but it is the verb. 'crash' rearranges DUE into EDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone is to teach or school them, to train them.

clue.text: Sweet child about to surface, surrounded by fish

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the reversed about word inside the fish

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising to the surface means reading upward, so the word is reversed

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A sweet child is about to come up for air among the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to surface' looks like 'on the point of rising', but RE (about) reads upwards as ER inside CHUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is an angelic winged child, so a sweet, innocent-looking child.

clue.text: Phone about current activity on track

indicators.note: about means around, so the phone word goes round the current abbreviation

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Someone phones about what is going on at a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current activity' reads as what is happening now, but 'current' is AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing is the sport of competing at speed, as horses or cars do on a track.

clue.text: Go back East, following a strange creed

indicators.note: following means the East letter comes after the rearranged creed
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters of creed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone returns to the East after joining an odd belief system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges CREED into RECED, with E after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to withdraw or move backward.

clue.text: Hope a din at sea is this foghorn

indicators.note: at sea means confused or lost, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the noise heard out on the water is a foghorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the maritime picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaphone is a type of foghorn producing a deep two-tone sound.

clue.text: Although off-colour I mean to go through with it

parts.note: read as a speaker who, despite feeling pale and unwell, intends to carry on: the words 'I am pale' run together

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell insists they will still see a task through.
explanation.walkthrough: Run together, the claim 'I'm pale' (off-colour) gives the letters; 'go through' then means pierce, not complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or run something through with a sharp point.

clue.text: For him, the biggest portion

parts.note: the idiom about the largest share of anything, named after the king of beasts in Aesop's fable

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the lion's share' means the biggest part, so the beast it is named after is the one who gets it.

clue.text: It is covered in blood and is swelling

indicators.note: covered in puts the word it inside the blood word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wound covered in blood is swelling up.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is a swelling of the neck caused by an enlarged thyroid gland.

clue.text: Approve of sage, moreover

parts.note: to like something is to approve of it
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Someone backs a wise person's view, and adds more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' could be the herb, but here it is the adjective, wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means also, in addition, similarly.

clue.text: Opening bottle — the contents Chinese port

indicators.note: the contents of a bottle are inside it, so the answer is the letters inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone opens a bottle of Chinese port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink, fitting the bottle, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ningbo is a major seaport city in Zhejiang province, eastern China.

clue.text: Persuade Nigel I've reformed

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells Nigel they have changed their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or wheedle someone into doing something.
